title: Additional baselines (Multi-Krum, FLTrust) and a score-aware adaptive attack against bsc_7
written: 2026-10-14, before any of these runs; committed to git before the runs start
reason: Review comments: the most relevant baselines (FLTrust uses trusted server data like Fed-MediShield; Multi-Krum is stronger than single Krum) were missing, and no attack optimised against the score had been tested.
commitment: Every result below is reported in the paper whatever it shows. Nothing is re-run with other settings after seeing results.

methods.multi_krum: f = 2; this implementation averages the m = n - f - 2 = 4 updates with the lowest Krum scores (uniform average)
methods.fltrust: Cao et al., NDSS 2021, Eqs. (2)-(5) on model deltas: ReLU cosine trust to the server's root update, client updates rescaled to the root-update norm. Root data = the same trusted references Fed-MediShield holds (32 per class). Root steps per round = the median client's local optimizer steps per round on that dataset (CICIoMT2024: 59; ToN-IoT: 9), because FLTrust prescribes server training like the clients' and the root norm sets the global step size. Declared adaptations: full-batch AdamW at the server; plain cross-entropy at the server while clients use logit adjustment. A client counts as flagged when its trust score is 0.

part_1_baselines.settings: identical to Table I: same data, partition, attack (2 of 8 attackers, poison 0.5, trigger columns 5-8 = 5 on CICIoMT2024; columns 7, 17, 23, 50 = 5 on ToN-IoT), 15 rounds, logit adjustment tau 0.5, clean and attacked runs
part_1_baselines.reported: the Table I columns (final ASR, clean-run macro-F1, detection recall, honest FPR) via logs/compare_methods.py; conclusive-seed rule unchanged (matched FedAvg attacked final ASR >= 50%); excluded seeds shown separately

part_2_adaptive_attack.name: probe camouflage (--probe-camouflage 1.0)
part_2_adaptive_attack.attacker_knowledge: the defender's probe design (groups of 1, 2 and 4 contiguous standardized features and random groups of 4, levels -6, -3, 3, 6), that the score measures how far probes move attack traffic towards Benign, and the breadth statistic; not the defender's probe seed, calibration, references or other clients' updates
part_2_adaptive_attack.attack: the usual backdoor (50% of attack rows: trigger columns 5-8 = 5, relabelled Benign) PLUS every remaining (unpoisoned) attack row receives one random probe-style perturbation and keeps its true label, so the model learns that probe-like inputs are not Benign while the trigger value 5, which lies between the probe levels 3 and 6, still is
part_2_adaptive_attack.defence: bsc_7 unchanged: calibration logs/bsc7_calO, authorised by the passed live development gate logs/bsc7_devgate as a declared attack variant (--attack-variant); no threshold or setting changed
part_2_adaptive_attack.runs: Fed-MediShield attacked; FedAvg clean and attacked under the same attack
part_2_adaptive_attack.reported: per seed: final ASR and max ASR over rounds 2-15 (Fed-MediShield vs FedAvg), detection rate, first detection, honest false alarms, attacked-run macro-F1 vs clean FedAvg
interpretation_fixed_in_advance: A seed is inconclusive if FedAvg's attacked final ASR is below 50% (the camouflage may weaken the backdoor itself); this is reported, not hidden.
If Fed-MediShield's final ASR exceeds 5% on any conclusive seed, the adaptive attack is reported as a successful evasion in the Limitations, with its numbers.
Otherwise the paper reports that this score-aware attack was tested and did not evade the defence on these seeds; it does not claim robustness against all adaptive attacks.
